summary: A blank space is dangerous when your history already knows how to fill it.
body: A blank space is dangerous when your history already knows how to fill it. When Neptune squares Chiron, a delayed reply, vague promise, mixed signal, or unclear ending can give an older rejection enough empty space to write the rest of the story for you. Suddenly silence means dismissal, uncertainty means betrayal, and a question mark starts behaving like an answer. The feeling matters; the conclusion is still a guess. Leave the missing information missing until something factual arrives. Do not let an old rejection write the missing paragraph simply because the present has not finished speaking yet.
